question_type: log growth between two year-end values of a bank-reported liabilities series whose endpoints are revised across several later issues (vintage choice)
decisive_step: Taking the latest revised printing of each year-end value of the Capital Movements row 'Total liabilities to all foreigners' (Table CM-I-1, Liabilities to Foreigners Reported by Banks): for end-2002 the second restatement printed under the column header 'Calendar Year 2002' in the 2004_03-2004_09 issues (worklog Step 5; 2004_03.txt:2605-2607), not the preliminary 'Dec. p' of 2003_03 or the first 'r' restatement of 2003_12; for end-2012 the 'Calendar Year 2012 r' column of the Dec 2013 issue (worklog Step 4; 2013_12.txt:2820-2822), not the 2013_03 preliminary or the 2013_09 revised value. Which table you start from matters only because it decides whether the tool can follow the cell to that last printing: CM-I-1 (a) can be followed; Chart CM-A (b) loses its caption in 2013_12; CM-I-3 (c) is a one-off preliminary snapshot.

a.path_summary: Its near-literal query returned 0 groups (a[5]); a shorter one matched CM-I-1 but only the 1982-2001 group fit in the 8000-byte page (a[7]); a title query led it to IFS-2 (a[9]), where it spent a[12]-a[34] on show_table/printings friction and computed a candidate from the IFS-2 total row (a[33]-a[34]) that it did not answer. At a[35] it doubted the wording, ran the FTS helper (four attempts, a[36]-a[42]), then a find_tables on 'Total Liabilities by Type of Holder' restricted to 2002-2013 (a[44]) which listed the modern CM-I-1 group. show_table showed the exact row label (a[46]-a[48]); printings on both 'Calendar Year' columns (a[51]) listed every restatement with its header and said 'latest printing'; calc at a[53]; answered at a[55] after checking the section name against the question (a[54]).

tool_use.friction: a[5] 0 hits for a query that contains the exact row label (find_tables searches title/header only unless --rows); a[7] page cut after 63 issue lines of the old CM-I-1 group, hiding the 2002-2013 group; a[12] exit 2 (show_table has no --table option); a[17] sed on a bare filename printed nothing; a[21] printings --row 2012 found no row in IFS-2 (Dec 2012 is a month row); a[26]-a[30] three calls to understand --from-row paging; a[36]-a[42] four python attempts to iterate officeqa.search() (returns a dict with 'results'), one exit 1.

b.path_summary: find_tables on the section wording returned only 1970s contents-page groups before the page cut (b[6]); with --years 2012-2013 it got IFS-2 and 'CHART CM-A' listed for 2012_12 and 2013_09 only (b[8]). It read IFS-2 (b[11], b[28]) and the chart (b[15]), decided the chart's 'Grand total' is the series (b[21], b[27]), and ran printings --table CM-A three times (b[22], b[24], b[26]); the title-token match pulled hundreds of unrelated 'Grand total' cells and each page was cut, but b[26]'s tail did show a single 'Calendar years > 2012' printing (2013_09). An rg for the literal row phrase (b[30]) returned 73 KB of header rows, truncated, and the CM-I-1 hits were not followed. It read the 2013_09 chart and a 2004_06 chart with show_table (b[32]), computed the log ratio (b[35]) and submitted once; recorded with no finding (b[37]).

Its end-2002 value matched the final restatement, so the answer was about 0.1% off.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: a used the CM-I-1 row by id, whose 2013_12 printing keeps its title, and printings listed 'Calendar Year 2012 r' in 2013_12 as the latest printing (a[51]); the reference tracked the same cell through 2013_03, 06, 09 and 12 and cross-checked CM-I-2 and the untitled chart in 2013_12 (worklog Step 4; 2013_12.txt:2822, :3029, :3190).

The consequence is a vintage error: both endpoints are the preliminary values, which for 2002 sit far below the later restatements.

smallest_change.change: Link untitled table reprints to their titled twin so printings (and the later_printing rule) can follow a cell into an issue where the caption was lost. In otables indexing: when a table part has no title/id, fingerprint it by section, units/banner line, row-label set and column-header pattern, and if a titled table in an earlier issue of the same section matches, give it that table's id with a flag. Model-visible effect on b[26] (printings --table CM-A --row 'Grand total' --col 2012): one more listing line '2013_12  treasury_bulletin_2013_12.txt:3190  p1 -  'Grand total' | c4 'Calendar years > 2012' = <value> [untitled; linked to CHART CM-A by shape]' and the SUMMARY block '[-] part1 calendaryears2012: 2 printings, 2 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings ... latest printing 2013_12 (treasury_bulletin_2013_12.txt:3190)'. find_tables would likewise show 'CHART CM-A ... 3 issues 2012_12..2013_12' at b[8]. With the same link, the later_printing rule would have fired at b[37] with a substitute_printing Offer.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a followed CM-I-1 by id, which keeps its title in every issue; the link only adds printings lines, and the flag makes the inference visible. A wrong shape match would add a mislabelled line, so the fingerprint should require the same row-label set and column count.

notes: Tool facts checked in the source: find_page searches {title header} only unless --rows, groups by (id, normalised title) so a title change ('Type of Holder' to 'Type and Holder') splits CM-I-1 into two groups, and with --all prints one line per part before the 8000-byte cap (a[7] lost the modern group). _printing_parts matches --table by id or by title tokens, so 'CM-A' as a title-token query pulled 'Grand total' rows from every capital-movements table (b[22]-b[26]); untitled parts have no id and cannot be reached. Verified in the corpus that the 2013_12 chart copy at line 3190 has no caption line while the 2013_09 copy at line 2573 does. Other v10 points: show_table for multi-part tables shows part 1 only and --from-row beyond part 1 returns an empty page (c[18], c[26]), so the grand total of CM-I-3 was unreachable through the tool; IFS-2's 'Total (1)' row is a near-miss decoy that a computed a candidate from (a[33]-a[34]) before doubting it, and its annual rows stop at 2011 so --row 2012 finds nothing (a[21]); the README's officeqa.py example should show that search() returns a dict with 'results' (a[36]-a[42], c[10]). The CM-I-2 grand total in 2013_12 (line 3029) and the untitled chart (line 3190) both carry the final 2012 value, so a row-label-plus-column-header search across the section would also have caught b's miss.
